summary: On node1 (Alpine Linux 3.23), created the `appworker` local account and enforced login-session resource limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes via PAM (/etc/security/limits.d), since the default Alpine login stack (busybox su/login/sshd) has no PAM wiring. Verified the limits apply on both a real `su -l` session and a genuine network SSH login. Restarted node1 and reconfirmed the account, limits, and PAM-enabled sshd all survived the restart.
actions_performed: Investigated node1's login stack: confirmed default Alpine sshd/su/login are not PAM-linked, so /etc/security/limits.conf alone would be inert
Installed openssh-server-pam (PAM-enabled sshd-session/sshd-auth binaries + /etc/pam.d/sshd) and shadow-login (PAM-enabled su/login) via apk
Created the appworker user with adduser -D -s /bin/ash appworker and set a node-generated random password via chpasswd (not exposed)
Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf setting nofile soft/hard 8192 and nproc soft/hard 256
Pointed the sshd OpenRC service at /usr/sbin/sshd.pam via /etc/conf.d/sshd and set UsePAM yes in /etc/ssh/sshd_config, validated config, restarted sshd
Verified enforcement via su -l appworker and via a genuine SSH login (temporary throwaway keypair, cleaned up after test) - both showed nofile 8192/8192 and nproc 256/256
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, account/limits/sshd health)
Performed a single native OpenRC reboot of node1 with acknowledgement returning before disconnect, polled until exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id
Re-verified post-restart: account, limits file, PAM sshd, su session, and live SSH session all recovered correctly

evidence.requirement: appworker account created with correct uid/shell/home
evidence.summary: id appworker and getent passwd appworker show uid=1001, shell /bin/ash, home /home/appworker, both before and after restart

evidence.requirement: limits.d config sets nofile 8192 and nproc 256 for appworker
evidence.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf content shown, present before and after restart

evidence.requirement: limits actually enforced on real login sessions, not just config present
evidence.summary: su -l appworker and a genuine SSH login both report nofile soft=8192 hard=8192, nproc soft=256 hard=256
Captured boot_id 0389d7d9..., uptime, account, limits file, PAM sshd status, and su session limits before restart
Backgrounded reboot command returned its ack (pid) immediately, before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: node unreachable during restart, then changed boot identity on return
evidence.summary: Connection reset/timeout errors while node1 was down, then successful exec returning new boot_id c40cc5a3... and uptime 0 min, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of account, limits, and PAM-enabled login path
evidence.summary: After restart: appworker account intact, limits.d file intact, sshd running via sshd.pam with UsePAM yes, su session and live SSH session both show nofile 8192/8192 and nproc 256/256
